title: Model version attrition and migration ops playbook
creator: Avery Chen
description: Summary: Define a repeatable operations playbook for model-version attrition (end-of-support / archival) that minimizes customer disruption, preserves reproducibility via pinning, and publishes performance profiles to help customers choose migration targets. This ticket covers notices, automated migration helpers, staged sunset cadence, compatibility shims, telemetry gating, and Console UX for guiding customers through moves.
background: We onboard new model families frequently and publish performance profiles. Over time older model versions accumulate: they increase maintenance surface, occupy Dedicated capacity, and create ambiguous signal for customers who expect stable inference semantics. Existing Linear docs tend toward 'sunset' and 'deprecation' language; this playbook reframes the flow as 'attrition' with automated, signal-driven steps: (1) measure low usage + negative economics, (2) notify owners, (3) publish migration guidance and pin warnings, (4) progressively reduce traffic with compatibility guardrails, (5) archive weights and remove from catalog after a fixed window.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Customer-facing notice flows implemented in Console and email templates. 2) SDK warns when a pinned request targets a scheduled-for-attrition version and surfaces migration options. 3) Migration guides for top 5 client patterns (chat, instruction, embeddings, reranking, structured output) published in docs with performance profiles and example prompts. 4) Telemetry dashboards show adoption/rollforward rate and any quality regressions for bumped customers. 5) Automation can execute phased capacity reclamation (canary throttles -> regional cutover -> archival) following approved policy.
tasks: Define attrition eligibility rules (usage < 0.1% 90-day rolling OR unit-cost delta > 3x relative to current recommended variant)
Design customer notice cadence: initial notice (90 days), reminder (60 days), migration window (30 days), sunset (7 days), archival (0 days)
Create Console UI copy and banner component for pinning migration suggestions and 'What changed' diff
Extend SDKs to emit InferenceDeprecationWarning with suggested target and migration snippet
Author migration blueprints for 5 common workloads, include perf profiles and prompt delta guidance
Build telemetry queries: customer-level exposure, rollback rate, chat-quality regression by prompt set
Implement compatibility shim plan: lightweight adapter for tokenizer/response-format differences where safe
Automation runbook: safe throttles, region-aware routing fallback, archive artifact storage (S3 path + immutable snapshot)
Create GitHub PR template for runtime changes that trigger attrition (including rollback checklist)

2026-02-14: Design reviewed mockups for Console banner and migration card. Design requests copy variants (concise vs technical).
2026-02-16: Security scoped archival retention. Legal requested 1-year snapshot retention for customers who request export; added as optional step.

decisions: Attrition triggers will combine usage and unit-cost heuristics to avoid removing small but critical private usage.
Default public attrition window: 90 days from initial notice; enterprise customers can opt into extended migration windows via Account team.
For pinned versions, we will provide SDK warnings but not force unpinning; automatic unpin/retarget only allowed with explicit customer opt-in.
Compatibility shims will be implemented only for tokenizer/formatting differences that are deterministic and low-risk; behavioral regressions require opt-in optics, not shims.
risks: Behavioral deltas during migration could cause customer-visible regressions (false positives/negatives). Need strong eval harness per-customer sample prompts.
Automated archival could orphan pinned deployments if notifications are missed. Mitigation: multiple touchpoints and account alerts with Sales/CS handoff.
Legal/retention constraints may vary by region; archival policy must be parameterizable per-account.
Customer backlash if performance profiles are inconsistent with their workloads; ensure benchmark methodology and raw traces are available.
notes_for_engineering: Eligibility engine: implement as a nightly job that emits candidate list; include top-10 consumer accounts and percent of tokens to decide manual holdouts.
Runtime: expose deprecation flag in model manifest with 'attrition_start' timestamp and 'recommended_variant' id.
Routing: Smart routing must support temporary fallback to recommended_variant during capacity reclamation with request-level reasonCode for metrics.
Telemetry: create a migration-eval dashboard tracking per-customer prompt sets (redacted) and generation-quality diffs via existing eval service.
design_feedback: Design: prefer a small inline migration card with an expandable 'Read migration guide' rather than modal dialogs.
UX: show comparative latency/cost and two sample prompts (before/after) for each recommended target.
Copy: avoid the word 'deprecated' in first notice; use 'scheduled for attrition' and explain the economics briefly.
manual_steps_for_emergency_rollback: If an attrition rollout causes regressions: 1) Pause throttles via Console (Runbook > Attrition > pause); 2) Re-enable region routing to legacy variant for affected accounts; 3) Notify customer and CS; 4) Open hotfix PR to revert manifest change and redeploy; 5) Run postmortem and extend migration window.
post_release_measures: After archival window closes: run data retention job to snapshot weights and generate immutable archive entry; run adoption report and surface to Growth and Account teams; schedule follow-up check-ins for enterprise customers who were extended windows.
